column3: MT 2:2. Close to the Hebrew; “guard the fortification” is rendered “Man the fort!”, and “strengthen the loins” “Strengthen your flanks!”

MT 2:4. NKJV renders “the chariots [are] in the fire of steel” as “The chariots come with flaming torches,” and “the cypresses are made to quiver” as “the spears are brandished”; the meaning is uncertain.
MT 2:6. Close to the Hebrew; “the cover” is rendered “the defense.”

MT 2:8. NKJV renders the uncertain opening (“it is fixed; it is uncovered; it is taken away”) as “It is decreed： She shall be led away captive, She shall be brought up,” and “moaning” as “shall lead her”; the meaning is uncertain.
MT 2:9. Close to the Hebrew; “from the days of it” is rendered “of old,” and NKJV supplies “they cry.”
MT 2:10. Close to the Hebrew; “there is no end to the supply” is rendered “There is no end of treasure.”
MT 2:11. Close to the Hebrew; “emptiness and emptiness and devastation” is rendered “She is empty, desolate, and waste,” and “all loins” “every side.”
MT 2:13. Close to the Hebrew; “its holes” is rendered “his caves.”
MT 2:14. Close to the Hebrew; “its chariotry” is rendered “your chariots.”
